newsitem.title: UK: China importance 'immense' for HSBC - Bond.
newsitem.headline: China importance 'immense' for HSBC - Bond.

text.p: China has an "immense" strategic importance for banking giant HSBC Holdings but its business can only be expanded at a pace allowed by the Chinese government, HSBC chief executive John Bond said on Wednesday.

"China is of immense strategic importance to our group," Bond said in an interview. "We want to expand our business in China but we want to expand in a way that's entirely consistent with the wishes of the regulatory authorities."
HSBC has the largest foreign bank presence in China and was one of the first to be allowed to do business in China's yuan currency since March of this year.
Previously, HSBC was only allowed to transact foreign currency business such as trade finance and foreign currency lending.
Bond said business is profitable and growing but has the potential in the decades ahead to become of major importance.

"We're growing the business in a very orderly fashion," Bond said. "They are allowing foreign banks gently to do more. Clearly, they want enough foreign bank competition to provide a stimulus to the banking system but not so much that it does any more than that."
Bond said HSBC's relations with the Chinese authorities were good and contacts were frequent.

He said the West does not really understand the "enormous achievement" of China to move from a planned to a much more market-oriented economy and praised the feat of keeping growth going and inflation down.
